title: Payoff Statements and Release of the Deed of Trust on Home Mortgage Loans
content:
A payoff statement on a Home Mortgage Loans note is sent within the program's stated number of business days of the request, free of charge, the statement fee on every program being nil.

**What the statement shows.** Principal, interest through the payoff date, fees due, and any escrow advance on the loan.

**What a payoff is.** A payment of at least the amount the statement shows posts as a payoff and moves the loan to paid off.

**After the payoff.** The satisfaction of the deed of trust is recorded within the program's stated number of calendar days, and the escrow balance remaining on the loan is refunded to the borrower.

## The statement in summary

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Turnaround | Within the program's stated business days of the request |
| Charge | None, the program's statement fee being nil |
| Principal | The principal outstanding |
| Interest | Through the payoff date |
| Fees | The fees due on the loan |
| Escrow | Any escrow advance on the loan |

## Worked reading on hypothetical inputs

A statement shows principal of $184300.00, interest through the payoff date of $612.40, fees due of $75.00 and an escrow advance of $430.00, which together come to $185417.40. A payment of $185417.40 is at least that amount and posts as a payoff; so would a payment of $185500.00. A payment of $185000.00 is less than the amount the statement shows and is not a payoff of it.

Because the turnaround is counted in business days and the recording deadline in calendar days, the two are counted on different bases even where the figures against them are read from the same schedule.
